target: The wall thickness of the absorber is 68 mm after the corrosion allowance is added, and the allowance is inside that figure rather than additional to it. For the gasket, two materials are compared on temperature limit only. Neither is assessed here on any other property, and the comparison gives no ranking on sealing, on life or on cost. On temperature limit the second material is preferred. Its rating stands higher, so the excursion the absorber can impose on the joint stays inside the rated range with room to spare, where the first material runs closer to its limit under the same excursion. The preference is narrow in scope: it decides the gasket on the one property the service presses hardest, and it leaves the remaining properties of both materials unexamined. The service at the joint is set by the excursions the absorber imposes rather than by its steady state, and a rating that only just covers the steady state leaves the excursion to be absorbed by whatever margin the material has, which is what the temperature limit speaks to.
